newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada sees Chilean free trade deal soon.
newsitem.headline: Canada sees Chilean free trade deal soon.

text.p: Canada and Chile should be able to reach a free trade agreement soon, Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Wednesday.

The two countries are negotiating a deal together in absence of the United States, which had been dragging its feet on bringing Chile into the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) that links Canada, the United States and Mexico.
"I think it's within reach. I don't think it's too far away, but we're not there yet," Eggleton told reporters. "I'm hopeful it'll happen soon."
He said Chilean negotiators arrived last Friday and would stay in Ottawa "hopefully until we get it done."

A visit to Canada by President Eduardo Frei which had been postponed in September partly because the agreement was not ready was now rescheduled for November, he said, adding that it would be great if an accord could be signed at that time.
